_comment: The scaffold contract as data. `checked` is upstream's pinned bytes (sha256 per file);
`.github/project/scaffold_gate.py --pin` regenerates it from the upstream tree, so it is
never hand-typed. `tolerated` is the honest, ratcheted list of template-owned files this
project forks, each with what removes the fork. Not in this tier: `.github/project/**`
(this contract and every project gate live there), `.include-guard.txt` (a derived project
states its own layering), `.github/skills/**` (agent guidance is project-specific), and every
content path -- README, metadata.json, include/, src/, api/, benchmark/ sources, docs,
test_package/test/**. See workspace/audit/gaps.md G-10/G-24 for why the template's own

`tolerance_budget` tracks the number of forks that actually exist: it was 3 at birth, 4 while the CMakeLists fork stood, back to 3 when that fork was reverted, and 2 now that the board-matrix entry turned out to be a deploy contract rather than a fork. Raising it is the one edit that must never be made to turn a gate green; it needs the owner's explicit sign-off, outside a feature commit.

tolerated.why: the first job must call the project-owned gate (.github/project/scaffold_gate.py); upstream's own check cannot accept any declared fork
tolerated.exit: drop the entry once the orchestrator step is upstreamed to fcpp v0.4+ and the template's check honours `tolerated`

tolerated.why: HETAI_PLAN_ROOT pointed at the upstream author's machine path /home/fcpp/WorkProject/Plan (IDENTITY_LEAK, gaps G-24)
tolerated.exit: none needed after this commit: the value now comes from the `vars.HETAI_PLAN_ROOT` repository variable, matching the two sibling env vars

tolerated.why: the coverage collector copies every .gcda/.gcno by basename into one flat directory, so two sources that share a file name overwrite each other and the loser silently vanishes from the report -- measured: five register.c and, after the x86 tier landed, six more names, which dropped core from 588 to 491 lines and pushed `all` under its floor (gaps G-62)
tolerated.exit: delete this entry, the patch file and section F1 of .github/project/scaffold-forks.md once upstream gives each object directory its own slot (or stops copying the pairs altogether), and put tolerance_budget back to 2

tolerated.why: the scaffold models feature toggles as metadata flags but has no way to make a requirement conditional on one, and no way for a flag to contribute a compile definition. The patch adds a generic injection point: `metadata.json:compile_options` maps an option name to the requirement it gates, the dependency key to drop while it is off, and the defines it contributes. Deliberately says nothing about any particular vendor -- this repository instantiates it, the scaffold does not know it exists.
tolerated.exit: drop this entry when upstream ships an equivalent compile-option mechanism; the data stays here either way, since metadata.json is this project's own surface

tolerated.why: the same generic point on the build side: `COMPILE_DEFINES` arrives from the Conan toolchain and is applied to the C target, so an option reaches the compiler without CMake learning any option's name
tolerated.exit: drop this entry together with the conanfile.py one, when upstream ships the hook

tolerated.why: the schema has additionalProperties:false, so the injection point needs its contract declared there: what a compile_options entry may contain. Without this the mechanism would be undocumented and metadata.json would fail validation.
tolerated.exit: drop this entry with the other two when upstream ships the hook; it is the same patch, not a separate decision

LICENSE.why: the Apache-2.0 text as shipped by fcpp v0.3.11; never modified since the initial commit -- pinning it here is how "do not touch the template text" stops being policy only

NOTICE.why: the template's licence statement, including the CC BY-NC 4.0 clause for the documentation; third-party attribution belongs in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, which this repository owns
